Simulated Smart Kanban Bins

A Modbus-to-Cloud IIoT Architecture for Pharmacy Replenishment
Load cells under Kanban bins see a reorder-point crossing as it happens, instead of waiting for the next stock report.
Diego Bethancourth¹ ² · Febylina Rumwaropen¹ · Dhansukh Jaladi¹
¹ School of Manufacturing Systems and Networks, Arizona State University
² Dirección Nacional de Logística (DINALOG), Caja de Seguro Social, Panama
MFG 598 Industrial Internet of Things · Fall 2026 · Instructor: Dr. Farhad AmeriGroup 2 · Final presentation · December 2, 2026

1. Problem Overview and Objectives

Medicine stock at Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) facilities is known only at report time; the reorder decision can wait for the next report.

Real-world problem

Panama's Social Security Fund (Caja de Seguro Social, CSS) replenishes its 71 health facilities across the country with procedure P-240. A facility's stock is known only when its SALMI stock report (the warehouse management system) is uploaded. A reorder-point crossing between two reports stays invisible until the next one.
71CSS health facilities
across Panama
109report dates in 159 days
(UE-A, 8 Jun – 13 Nov 2026)
6shortlisted medicines,
3 of them vital
20days of P-240
lead time L

P-240 reorder point (already used by the CSS dashboard)

SS=zσdLROP=d‾L+SS
d̄, σd: mean and standard deviation of daily demand (last 90 days) · z = 1.65 vital items, 1.28 other items · L = 20 days
What the prototype demonstrates
  1. Simulate six load-cell bins that replay the real SALMI stock series, with sensor faults.
  2. Connect Modbus TCP (device → edge) and MQTT 5.0 over TLS (edge → cloud).
  3. Decide at the edge: grams → units, P-240 reorder with hysteresis, fault flags, store-and-forward.
  4. Store and show in InfluxDB Cloud and a Grafana dashboard.
  5. Measure how much earlier a sensed crossing is seen than the report that shows it.
WHY IIoT IS NEEDEDThe rule already exists; what is missing is observation. Continuous sensing, an edge that applies the rule on site, and a cloud record turn a periodic snapshot into an event.
Scope: simulation only; no change to CSS systems. Facility anonymised as UE-A.

2. System Architecture: Five IIoT Layers

One chain, end to end. Every box is running code in the repository, started with docker compose up.

SIMULATED vs REALOnly the load cells are simulated. Modbus, Node-RED, EMQX Cloud, InfluxDB Cloud and Grafana are the real services.
SECURITY ACROSS LAYERSModbus stays inside the facility LAN; everything leaving it is TLS with a verified certificate and per-user credentials.
ONE COMMANDdocker compose up starts simulator, edge, ingest and dashboard; a local profile runs it without internet.
MFG 598 IIoT · Group 2 · All sensors are simulated; communication, edge rules and cloud services are real.

3a. Physical Device Layer: Simulated Load Cells

Six bins on load cells, one Modbus device each, weighing the real SALMI stock history of facility UE-A.

Sensors and data

6 load cells, Modbus unit IDs 1–6, one register map. Gross weight in mg (uint32), status, simulated time. Read every 1 s; 1 simulated day = 10 s.

How we ensured realism

Stock equals the SALMI report on all 109 report dates (8 Jun – 13 Nov 2026, 27 automated tests). Between reports, Poisson-like dispensing adds up exactly to the observed drop. Tare, unit weight, scale factor, noise 0.2 g.
RegisterContent
40001-2gross weight, mg
40003status 0 / 1
40004-5simulated minutes
40006replay cycle
MFG 598 IIoT · Group 2 · simulator/replay.py, simulator/server.py · docs/register_map.md

3b. Network / Communication Layer

Modbus TCP inside the facility; MQTT 5.0 over TLS from the edge to the cloud.

FIELDModbus TCP

Port 5020 · function code 3 (read holding registers) · 6 registers per unit ID · 32-bit values high word first.

UPLINKMQTT 5.0 over TLS

  • Port 8883, server certificate verified; fallback WSS 8084 (both tested open on campus Wi-Fi)
  • QoS 1 (at least once), keep-alive 30 s, user and password
  • Retained level: a new subscriber gets the last value at once
  • Birth / close / last will on the gateway status topic
WHY MQTTPublish/subscribe decouples edge and cloud; the payload is small JSON; the broker itself reports a lost gateway.
# topic structure
css/UE-A/bins/{bin01…bin06}/level    retained
css/UE-A/bins/{bin}/reorder
css/UE-A/bins/{bin}/epcis
css/UE-A/edge/gw01/status    online | offline

  "units": 4001,  "grams": 1600.2,
  "status": 0,  "flag": "ok",  "rop": 2863.6,
  "sim_min": 2618,  "cycle": 0,  "heartbeat": false
}

3c. Edge / Gateway Layer: Node-RED

The reorder decision is taken at the edge, so it keeps working when the internet does not.

Aggregation

One Modbus client polls unit IDs 1 – 6 every second and decodes the 32-bit values.

Protocol translation

Registers → MQTT JSON.
units = round((g − tare) / unit) × k

Filtering and analytics

Deadband per bin, 60 s heartbeat. P-240 with hysteresis: one event per crossing, re-arm above ROP × 1.10.

Buffering

Store-and-forward queue on disk; sent in order on reconnect; the last 5 s are re-queued when the link drops.

Security

TLS with verified server certificate; credentials only in .env; birth, close and last will.
Flag, don't order. A sensor with status 1 (hard fault), or one whose raw value stays identical for 20 polls while demand says units should have gone (stuck), is published with status 1 / 2 and never triggers a reorder.
HOW IT FORWARDSMQTT out, QoS 1: level retained, reorder and epcis not retained, all stamped with the edge time.
MFG 598 IIoT · Group 2 · edge/flows.json · edge/lib/p240.js

3d. Cloud Platform Layer: EMQX Cloud and InfluxDB Cloud

Broker, ingest and time-series database; every point keeps the time it was measured at the edge.

MeasurementTagsFields
levelue, bin_id, itemunits, grams, status, rop, sim_min
reorderue, bin_id, itemunits, rop, ss, sim_min
gatewayue, gw_idonline 1 / 0 (birth, last will)

Data pipeline

Persistent session: the broker keeps QoS 1 messages while ingest is away. Each point takes the edge timestamp, so queued messages land at the right time.
ANALYTICSDetection latency: each sensed crossing against the first SALMI report at or below the same ROP (tools/latency.py, section 5).

3e. Application Layer: Dashboard, Alerts and EPCIS Events

What the pharmacy or the logistics directorate would see, and the event an ERP could receive.

What users see

Stock against the ROP line, the reorder events table, gateway ONLINE / OFFLINE with data age, and flagged bins.

How decisions show

One crossing → one event: a table row and a message on …/reorder. A flagged bin turns red and orders nothing.

MES / ERP function

The reorder is the Kanban signal for a P-240 requisition, also sent as a GS1 EPCIS 2.0 ObjectEvent:

3f. Application Layer: 3D Twin of the Whole Loop

From the load cell to the ERP requisition and back to the shelf, in one view laid out by ISA-95 level.

What it shows

Fill level per bin, gold ring = ROP, red when flagged; L3 pauses in an outage and backfills; L4 closes each requisition with its actual lead time.

Three data sources

Edge: Node-RED /ws/twin
Cloud: MQTT over WebSocket
Replay: SALMI series in the browser

Why it matters for CSS

One look tells a pharmacy chief or DINALOG what to reorder and which sensor to fix; a new shelf is a new entry in bins.yaml.

5.1 Challenges and Lessons Learned

Most problems were in the details that decide whether a count or a message can be trusted.

Major technical challenges
Resolution. Whole grams cannot tell one 0.3 g tablet from the next → registers in milligrams; floor lost a unit with −0.1 g of noise → round.
Silent loss. Node-RED's MQTT node drops a publish while disconnected and reports it a moment late → the buffer re-queues the last 5 s.
Dependencies. The Node-RED Modbus package downloads a dependency outside npm → the modbus-serial library in a function node. HiveMQ removed its free plan → EMQX.
Environment. Docker Desktop on Windows needs WSL; campus ports had to be tested before trusting TLS on 8883.
Most important insights about IIoT architecture
  1. Decide at the edge. The rule keeps working without internet, and the edge is the right place to stamp the time.
  2. Timestamp at the source, not at arrival. Late data is still correct data.
  3. Test the failure paths: outage, crash, stuck sensor. They are where IIoT systems differ from a script.
  4. Every parameter needs a source. bins.yaml records where each value comes from (SALMI, P-240, item dictionary, or a simulation choice).
  5. Use the broker's features: retained values, QoS 1 and the last will replace custom code.
THE RULE WE TAKE AWAYDecide, buffer and timestamp at the edge; the cloud records, and the dashboard shows.
MFG 598 IIoT · Group 2 · docs/decisions.md

6. Conclusion and Future Extensions

A sensing and edge layer that works with the replenishment rule CSS already uses, one hardware swap away from a real pharmacy.

Usefulness of the prototype

The chain sees a P-240 reorder-point crossing when it happens, keeps every reading through network outages, and flags a bad sensor instead of ordering. The gain grows where reports are less frequent; it adds observation without replacing SALMI or the existing dashboards.
From simulation to real hardware in one pharmacy
ALREADY IN INDUSTRIAL USEWeight-sensing smart bins exist today: Bossard SmartBin tracks parts with weight sensors in each bin, updates stock in the cloud and orders automatically at a reorder point.

Next extensions

  • Security and scale: per-device certificates (mutual TLS), many facilities on one broker
  • Forecasting: a demand forecast instead of the fixed 90-day d̄ in P-240
  • ERP link: EPCIS events into the requisition system, as in the twin's L4 screen
